t: Athens unified Attica and in 508/507 BCE created the democracy that let the citizen Assembly decide war, finance and law.
Its fleet won at Salamis in 480 BCE and led the Delian League, which Athens turned into a tribute-paying Aegean empire.
Defeated by Sparta in 404 BCE and dominated by Macedon after 338 BCE, it stayed the cultural capital of Greece until Sulla's sack.
dyk: Athenian jurors and many officials were chosen by lot; from the fourth century a stone allotment machine, the kleroterion, was used to assign citizens to courts at random.
ev: Solon's reforms cancel debts on the person and abolish debt bondage
Cleisthenes reorganises the citizen body and founds the democracy
The Athenian-led Greek fleet defeats Xerxes I at Salamis
Construction of the Parthenon begins under Pericles
Athens surrenders to Sparta at the end of the Peloponnesian War
Philip II of Macedon defeats Athens and Thebes at Chaeronea
Sulla storms Athens after it sides with Mithridates VI
